At first glance, one might dismiss this as a tragic cluster of unrelated misfortunes: heart attacks, hiking accidents, random crimes. But when the numbers climb to nine, and the victims share connections to national security-critical fields, it stops looking like pure coincidence and starts demanding serious scrutiny. **No one is rushing to wild conspiracy theories here.** Yet ignoring the pattern would be reckless, especially given how closely it echoes the targeted assassinations of Iranian nuclear scientists between 2010 and 2025.
Let's lay out the circumstances, one by one, based on reported facts. No embellishment--just the known details that have raised eyebrows among former FBI officials, members of Congress, and national security watchers.
Let's start with the NASA JPL cluster. Michael David Hicks, a 59-year-old research scientist at JPL, died on **July 30, 2023**. He had worked there for over two decades, publishing extensively on comets and asteroids, and contributed to projects like the DART asteroid deflection test and Deep Space 1. His cause of death was never publicly disclosed, and no autopsy record has surfaced.
**[Frank Maiwald,](https://substack.com/redirect/7c742994-f0eb-473e-b21f-568a1dbce97c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/7c742994-f0eb-473e-b21f-568a1dbce97c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)another longtime JPL principal researcher and coworker of Hicks, died on **July 4, 2024** , at age 61 in Los Angeles. Again, minimal public information, no known autopsy, and only a brief obituary noting his leadership on advanced satellite instruments for planetary observation.
**[Monica Jacinto Reza](https://substack.com/redirect/7dfd3732-b6c8-4daf-b87e-851c8f53a9f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , 60, who had just become Director of the Materials Processing Group at JPL. She co-invented "Mondaloy," a specialized nickel-based superalloy for advanced rocket engines and missile technology, with funding ties to the Air Force Research Laboratory. On **June 22, 2025** , while hiking in California's Angeles National Forest near Mount Waterman-- an experienced hiker just 30 feet from companions--she vanished. No body, no evidence, case unsolved. A premature online memorial claiming a "green burial" appeared and was later removed.
**[Melissa Casias](https://substack.com/redirect/9af8dc22-c757-4785-9562-164e30022107?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , 54, an administrative assistant at Los Alamos National Laboratory with prior national security clearance (later revoked over family finances), disappeared on **June 26, 2025** , in New Mexico. She dropped her husband at work, claimed she forgot her badge, returned home, factory-reset both phones, left everything behind, and walked off alone. She hasn't been seen since.
**[Nuno Loureiro](https://substack.com/redirect/7dfd3732-b6c8-4daf-b87e-851c8f53a9f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , 47, director of MIT's Plasma Science and Fusion Center, was shot dead in his Brookline, Massachusetts home on **December 15, 2025**. His work focused on breakthroughs in nuclear fusion energy and plasma physics with potential implications for advanced propulsion.
**[Jason Thomas](https://substack.com/redirect/7dfd3732-b6c8-4daf-b87e-851c8f53a9f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , 45, a pharmaceutical researcher at Novartis with Department of Defense and Health and Human Services contracts, disappeared in **December 2025** ; his remains were found in a Massachusetts lake on March 17, 2026. Cause undetermined.
**[Carl Grillmair](https://substack.com/redirect/7dfd3732-b6c8-4daf-b87e-851c8f53a9f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , 67, a Caltech astrophysicist with heavy NASA/JPL support, was shot dead on his front porch in Llano, California, on **February 16, 2026**. His research involved infrared telescopes (NEOWISE, NEO Surveyor) for asteroid tracking--technology with clear dual-use applications for monitoring satellites and hypersonic missiles. A suspect was charged, but questions linger about motive and possible prior surveillance of his property.
Finally, retired Air Force General **[William Neil McCasland](https://substack.com/redirect/7dfd3732-b6c8-4daf-b87e-851c8f53a9f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , 68, who had commanded research sites tied to advanced aerospace and once oversaw programs linked to Reza's work, vanished on **February 27, 2026** , near a hiking trail in Albuquerque, New Mexico. But the national security dimension cannot (**and should not**) be waved away. These individuals weren't working on consumer gadgets. Their expertise touched missile propulsion, nuclear fusion that could reshape energy (and potentially weapons), asteroid/comet deflection with defense overlaps, and materials that power next-generation rockets. Knowledge like that doesn't just walk out the door--it represents a strategic advantage for America and a problem for any rival power.
As individual cases these could be explained away, concerns brushed off, but the fact that they are **so tightly connected to such a sensitive and crucial industry and happened in such a short period of time** ought to raise red flags, if for no other reason than that this pattern bears more than a passing resemblance to what happened to Iran's nuclear scientists from 2010 to 2025.
In that campaign, prominent figures--nuclear engineers, physicists, and program leaders--were methodically eliminated through sticky bombs on motorcycles, shootings, and eventually overt strikes. No one publicly claimed responsibility for the early covert killings, though they were widely attributed to state-level operations aimed at slowing Iran's weapons program. Iran lost senior expertise, institutional memory, and momentum. The methods differed--covert deniability versus the more open 2025 airstrikes--but the goal was the same: degrade a strategic capability by removing irreplaceable human capital. Which leaves us with the uncomfortable question. Is someone running the same playbook against America's scientific community?
Here in the U.S., we're seeing unexplained deaths and disappearances in the fields that underpin American technological dominance in space, defense, and energy. No evidence yet points to foreign agents slipping in and out with silenced pistols or remote weapons. But the silence from agencies, the lack of transparent autopsies in some cases, and the clustering around dual-use technologies should prompt harder questions, not dismissal as paranoia.
**We don 't need to invent shadowy cabals or extraterrestrial angles to take this seriously.** Rivals like China, Russia, Iran, and others invest heavily in espionage to close technology gaps. Recruiting, pressuring, or eliminating key personnel has long been a tool of statecraft for centuries. Scientists and researchers today are a soft target with outsize importance to any country looking to hamper and hinder an adversaries technological advancement.
**The responsible course of action isn 't panic or conspiracy-mongering.** It's transparency and rigorous investigation. Families (and the public) deserve answers. The public, whose tax dollars fund these labs, deserves assurance that critical national assets aren't being quietly whittled away by a foreign power. Congress should demand briefings and the FBI and intelligence community need to connect dots across jurisdictions rather than treating each case in isolation. If patterns of surveillance, unusual financial activity, or foreign contacts emerge, they must be pursued without regard for institutional embarrassment and most importantly if there is evidence of a concerted plan to punch the ticket on America's scientific community then steps need to be taken to protect this unseen but vital community.
America's strength has always rested on innovation protected by vigilance. Losing even a handful of top minds in propulsion, fusion, and space surveillance isn't just a personnel issue--it's a potential erosion of deterrence and leadership.
Coincidence can explain a lot, but not everything. When the dead and missing all orbit the same constellation of America's most coveted secrets, it's time to stop looking away and start asking the tough questions before the list grows longer.

Friend, Last week, I was proud to officially launch the new **People’s Environmental Justice Caucus in Congress** , alongside environmental justice advocates and Congresswomen Summer Lee and Adelita Grijalva. This caucus is more needed than ever, as Trump gives corporations a free pass to pollute our communities and worsen the climate crisis. Under the Trump administration, the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has weakened air and water protections, rolled back environmental policies, and limited restrictions on greenhouse gases (which cause climate change). Meanwhile, government agencies charged with protecting our public lands have opened up more land to mining and fossil fuel extraction. Friend,
I represent Detroit, a majority-Black city that’s been named the “top asthma capital” of the country—mainly because of air pollution.
Black Americans are 30% more likely to have asthma than white Americans. In Detroit, Black residents are nearly four times more likely to be hospitalized due to asthma than white residents. This is environmental racism in action, tied to anti-Black housing and zoning policies.
Through years of organizing with the environmental justice community in Detroit, I’ve learned that our government has sacrificed our families’ health and lives so corporate polluters can profit. I’ve been fighting for our right to clean air and water my whole career, and I’ll keep fighting for environmental justice and bold climate action.
**Last week, I officially launched the People’s Environmental Justice Caucus in Congress** , alongside Congresswomen Summer Lee and Adelita Grijalva as well as frontline community leaders from across the country.
As Trump rolls back environmental protections and Congressional Republicans cut essential funding for programs to get lead out of drinking water, this caucus is more important than ever. We urgently need more members of Congress taking action for environmental justice.

I’ve taken on billionaire polluters before, including pushing the Koch brothers to fully clean up and remove toxic waste from Detroit’s riverfront. Now, I'm fighting back as Trump and his administration collaborate with corporations to undo our progress and pollute our communities.
Our fight for environmental justice includes protecting public health, ending racist policies, fighting discrimination, stopping new fossil fuel extraction, supporting renewable energy, addressing climate change’s impacts and the extreme weather it fuels, and more.
I’ve helped create a fund totaling $1.1 billion to help families access clean water, passed historic amendments that would provide $23 billion to fully replace dangerous lead pipes, and successfully worked with federal agencies to protect drinking water and reduce exposure to toxic chemicals.
And I’ll continue leading policies to ensure everyone can access clean water and utilities, strengthen our civil rights and anti-discrimination laws, end poverty and environmental racism, take on the fossil fuel industry, and expand affordable housing and keep people in their homes—including my legislation requiring FEMA to cover basement flood damage and life-saving mold and mildew remediation.
**The People’s Environmental Justice Caucus will serve as a platform for members of Congress to collaborate with community leaders, advocates, and policy experts to advance environmental justice legislation—and ensure that federal policies reflect the needs and priorities of the communities most impacted by environmental harm.**
Supporting the launch of our new caucus, the Climate Justice Alliance coalition noted: _“This is a historic step towards building the just climate future our communities deserve.”_
Dalal Aboulhosn of the Center for Earth, Energy & Democracy said: _“The formation of the House Environmental Justice Caucus is a critical step toward bringing frontline communities into policymaking and ensuring that public health is no longer secondary to corporate profits.”_

This is connected to our work to rein in military spending and stop federal lawmakers from profiting off war: The U.S. military is the biggest user of fossil fuels in the world, and the largest institutional emitter of greenhouse gases.
In the past month, the U.S. and Israeli governments’ carpet bombing of Iran and Lebanon has released millions of tons of climate-change-causing emissions—making the world less safe for all of us while poisoning lands, waters, and people for years to come.
We’re all connected, as are our movements for liberation. Although we’re up against powerful industries and government leaders, change always happens because the people demand it. Together we are powerful.

This caucus is more needed than ever, as Trump gives corporations a free pass to pollute our communities and worsen the climate crisis. Under the Trump administration, the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has weakened air and water protections, rolled back environmental policies, and limited restrictions on greenhouse gases (which cause climate change). Meanwhile, government agencies charged with protecting our public lands have opened up more land to mining and fossil fuel extraction. In Congress, my Republican colleagues have cut much-needed environmental justice funding, including programs I’ve championed to eliminate lead from our drinking water and help low-income families pay their increasingly unaffordable water bills. We must fight back against these attacks on our communities. | Thank you for taking action! My whole career, I’ve worked alongside environmental justice advocates in my hometown of Detroit—pushing to ensure the human right to access clean water and breathe clean air, and to hold corporate polluters accountable for endangering our health.** Please check out yesterday’s email for more information about my environmental justice work in Congress, and know that I’ll never back down in the fight for people and our planet over corporate greed. With you in the fight, Rashida \---------- Forwarded message --------- From: Rashida Tlaib**** Date: Wed, Apr 8, 2026 Subject: Sign to support the new People’s Environmental Justice Caucus: To: dpwillis67@gmail.com Friend, I represent Detroit, a majority-Black city that’s been named the “top asthma capital” of the country—mainly because of air pollution. Black Americans are 30% more likely to have asthma than white Americans. In Detroit, Black residents are nearly four times more likely to be hospitalized due to asthma than white residents. This is environmental racism in action, tied to anti-Black housing and zoning policies. Through years of organizing with the environmental justice community in Detroit, I’ve learned that our government has sacrificed our families’ health and lives so corporate polluters can profit. I’ve been fighting for our right to clean air and water my whole career, and I’ll keep fighting for environmental justice and bold climate action. Last week, I officially launched the People’s Environmental Justice Caucus in Congress , alongside Congresswomen Summer Lee and Adelita Grijalva as well as frontline community leaders from across the country. As Trump rolls back environmental protections and Congressional Republicans cut essential funding for programs to get lead out of drinking water, this caucus is more important than ever. We urgently need more members of Congress taking action for environmental justice. I’ve taken on billionaire polluters before, including pushing the Koch brothers to fully clean up and remove toxic waste from Detroit’s riverfront. Now, I'm fighting back as Trump and his administration collaborate with corporations to undo our progress and pollute our communities. Our fight for environmental justice includes protecting public health, ending racist policies, fighting discrimination, stopping new fossil fuel extraction, supporting renewable energy, addressing climate change’s impacts and the extreme weather it fuels, and more. I’ve helped create a fund totaling $1.1 billion to help families access clean water, passed historic amendments that would provide $23 billion to fully replace dangerous lead pipes, and successfully worked with federal agencies to protect drinking water and reduce exposure to toxic chemicals. And I’ll continue leading policies to ensure everyone can access clean water and utilities, strengthen our civil rights and anti-discrimination laws, end poverty and environmental racism, take on the fossil fuel industry, and expand affordable housing and keep people in their homes—including my legislation requiring FEMA to cover basement flood damage and life-saving mold and mildew remediation. The People’s Environmental Justice Caucus will serve as a platform for members of Congress to collaborate with community leaders, advocates, and policy experts to advance environmental justice legislation—and ensure that federal policies reflect the needs and priorities of the communities most impacted by environmental harm. Supporting the launch of our new caucus, the Climate Justice Alliance coalition noted: “This is a historic step towards building the just climate future our communities deserve.” Dalal Aboulhosn of the Center for Earth, Energy & Democracy said: “The formation of the House Environmental Justice Caucus is a critical step toward bringing frontline communities into policymaking and ensuring that public health is no longer secondary to corporate profits.” Thank you for being part of the fight for environmental and climate justice. Together we’ll keep fighting to change our government’s priorities and put people over corporate profits. This is connected to our work to rein in military spending and stop federal lawmakers from profiting off war: The U.S. military is the biggest user of fossil fuels in the world, and the largest institutional emitter of greenhouse gases. In the past month, the U.S. and Israeli governments’ carpet bombing of Iran and Lebanon has released millions of tons of climate-change-causing emissions—making the world less safe for all of us while poisoning lands, waters, and people for years to come. We’re all connected, as are our movements for liberation. Although we’re up against powerful industries and government leaders, change always happens because the people demand it. body:
We deserve elected officials who care about what matters to us.

| | | [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/1102?refcode=jtk553-fr-ndem-header&t=1&akid=8853%2E400544%2EqG9f4O)
---
Friend,

Since I first stepped into public service, I’ve known why I’m here: To make sure the people who’ve been overlooked finally have a seat at the table. Too often, the loudest voices and biggest donors set the agenda, while working families, rural communities, and folks just trying to get by, like I once was as a single mom, are left out.

That’s not right.
**No matter where you live, where you’re from, or what kind of job you hold, every New Mexican deserves to be heard and to see their needs reflected in the decisions that shape their lives.** As governor, I’ll lead the way I always have: listening first and fighting for the people who don’t have a seat at the table. **_[I’m running to represent all New Mexicans and give a voice to those who don’t have one. Please, will you chip in $5 to my campaign for governor so I can deliver progress to working families across our state?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/7312?refcode=jtk553-fr-nd&t=2&akid=8853%2E400544%2EqG9f4O)_**
| | [Donate](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/7312?refcode=jtk553-fr-nd&t=3&akid=8853%2E400544%2EqG9f4O)
---
Like my mother and her mother, I have always felt a deep responsibility to my state and our communities — it’s how and why I got my start as an Organizer.

---|---|---
Four British nationals were apprehended by U.S. Border Patrol agents in a remote stretch of Somerset County woods after illegally crossing from Canada into the United States on April 3, federal court documents filed this week reveal.
One of them captured the whole thing on a GoPro camera, narrating a celebration as the group set foot on American soil.
"I can confirm you are now on US Soil," Mohammed Sultan Saleh narrated on video as the group crossed through thick forest just a few hundred yards from the St. Zacharie Port of Entry in northwestern Somerset County, according to an affidavit sworn by U.S. Border Patrol Agent Scott Hanton and filed April 7 in U.S. District Court for the District of Maine.
Another man in the group -- Ali Mohammed Ali Abdullah -- can be heard on the recording asking, "I'm on US Soil?" Saleh replied by showing his phone screen with GPS coordinates displayed, and declared, "Now, we are in the US. We just made it, baby."
The bust began with an unlikely pair of informants: two maple sugar workers heading into Canada who spotted four men of apparent Middle Eastern appearance walking south along the Golden Road near mile marker 90 -- in the wrong direction to be casual hikers.

For those unfamiliar with the Golden Road, it's a 96-mile, primarily unpaved private logging road in Maine, stretching from Millinocket west to the Quebec border -- and there's nothing but trees to see for 95.9 of those miles and no cell service.
The unidentified maple sugar workers flagged down a U.S. Customs and Border Protection officer at the St. Zacharie Port of Entry at approximately 9:15 a.m. to alert them to the bizarre sighting.
By 9:40 a.m., the same workers had returned to the U.S. side with more intelligence: a third man had told them that two men in a gray Nissan parked on the Golden Road were asking passersby for fuel and Wi-Fi so they could contact the people they were supposed to pick up. At 10:13 a.m., that same third man called back -- the Nissan had turned up near his maple sugar shack at mile marker 80.
A Border Patrol agent and the CBP officer loaded up a marked patrol vehicle and headed south on the Golden Road. At mile marker 90, they spotted fresh footprints in the soft dirt. At mile marker 87, they found the men themselves -- four individuals attempting to conceal themselves in roadside vegetation.
Google Maps images of the area help show just how remote a location the supposed British hikers had found themselves in.
"One of the four men was acting nervously," Hanton wrote in his affidavit. "The two officers took the four men into custody without incident."
Although the Go Pro recording would show the men indisputably entered the U.S. illegally and intentionally, they initially claimed they were 'just going for a hike.'
When questioned about their citizenship, all four told agents they were British citizens. They claimed they didn't know they had entered the United States, a claim the Go Pro recording revealed to be a lie.
[Share The Robinson Report](https://substack..rPFzZnJukXOq5JNVPltQxzYQCjnhK-rdsrUl7aB3mCY?)
After being transported to the Jackman Border Patrol station, the men were identified as Ali Mohammed Ali Abdullah, 18, of Liverpool, England; Hameed Mohammed Nagi; Ibrahim Ayyub Khan; and Mohammed Sultan Saleh -- all British nationals, according to court documents.
Their stories didn't hold up.
Abdullah declined to answer questions. Nagi claimed he was just going on a hike with the group. Saleh echoed that line -- but federal agents had already found the GoPro footage on his phone, along with a series of telling Google searches conducted April 3: "bangor from my location," "boston from bangor," "new york from boston," and -- critically -- "is st zacharie border crossing still used the one near quebec golden road."
That last search would appear to put to rest any claim that Saleh was unaware he had crossed an international border.
The gray Nissan the maple sugar workers had described was still sitting near mile marker 80 when agents returned -- out of gas. Two men were inside. They identified themselves as U.S. citizens.
Before the driver could fully exit the vehicle, a CBP officer observed him reach under the driver's seat. When agents checked, they found a loaded 9mm handgun.
The two men in the Nissan were taken to Jackman as well, in connection with what the affidavit describes as "a suspected alien smuggling event." The passenger of the vehicle later admitted to investigators that the driver had intended to pick up one of the four men -- someone the driver said he had dropped off in the same Golden Road area approximately 30 days earlier, according to Homeland Security Investigations Special Agent Pierre Mathieu, who briefed Hanton.
A forensic review of the driver's cell phone found text messages with an individual believed to be one of the four men, discussing expected arrival times and pickup logistics, according to the court filing.
Federal prosecutors' motion for pretrial detention adds a further wrinkle to the story.
Abdullah, identified as the lead defendant in the criminal complaints, had previously run afoul of U.S. immigration authorities. His application to extend his U.S. visa was denied in March 2025, and he departed the country in May 2025, the motion states.
Prosecutors allege that Canadian authorities had recorded his arrival in Canada on April 1, 2026 -- two days before the Maine crossing -- traveling on a United Kingdom passport.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2246936&post_id=193717157&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTkzNzE3MTU3LCJpYXQiOjE3NzU3NTk3MDQsImV4cCI6MTc3ODM1MTcwNCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTIyNDY5MzYiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.Ub2DKVE2DZKLzNFBjga4E0D0i5bIWS3-Eb7utkDKy6M)
"Law enforcement authorities are attempting to ascertain the purpose of his travel to Maine," the motion states.
All four men are charged with one count each of Entry Without Inspection, a Class B misdemeanor under 8 U.S.C. § 1325(a)(1), which carries a maximum sentence of six months in federal prison and a $5,000 fine. The case is assigned to U.S. Magistrate Judge John C. Nivison.
Abdullah appeared before the court on April 7 and waived his right to both a preliminary hearing and a detention hearing, consenting to remain in federal custody pending trial. The court accepted his waiver and ordered him detained.
Trial is scheduled to begin June 3, 2026, before Magistrate Judge Nivison. Pretrial motions are due April 21.
The three co-defendants -- Nagi, Khan, and Saleh -- have related cases pending in the same district.

clean_body: British men Ali Mohammed Ali Abdullah, Hameed Mohammed Nagi, Ibrahim Ayyub Khan, and Mohammed Sultan Saleh were caught illegally sneaking into the U.S. in a remote part of Maine, per court records. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more ? British men Ali Mohammed Ali Abdullah, Hameed Mohammed Nagi, Ibrahim Ayyub Khan, and Mohammed Sultan Saleh were caught illegally sneaking into the U.S. in a remote part of Maine, per court records. Apr 9 | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Four British nationals were apprehended by U.S. Border Patrol agents in a remote stretch of Somerset County woods after illegally crossing from Canada into the United States on April 3, federal court documents filed this week reveal. One of them captured the whole thing on a GoPro camera, narrating a celebration as the group set foot on American soil. "I can confirm you are now on US Soil," Mohammed Sultan Saleh narrated on video as the group crossed through thick forest just a few hundred yards from the St. Zacharie Port of Entry in northwestern Somerset County, according to an affidavit sworn by U.S. Border Patrol Agent Scott Hanton and filed April 7 in U.S. District Court for the District of Maine. Another man in the group -- Ali Mohammed Ali Abdullah -- can be heard on the recording asking, "I'm on US Soil?" Saleh replied by showing his phone screen with GPS coordinates displayed, and declared, "Now, we are in the US. We just made it, baby." The bust began with an unlikely pair of informants: two maple sugar workers heading into Canada who spotted four men of apparent Middle Eastern appearance walking south along the Golden Road near mile marker 90 -- in the wrong direction to be casual hikers. Get the Robinson Report in your inbox... For those unfamiliar with the Golden Road, it's a 96-mile, primarily unpaved private logging road in Maine, stretching from Millinocket west to the Quebec border -- and there's nothing but trees to see for 95.9 of those miles and no cell service. The unidentified maple sugar workers flagged down a U.S. Customs and Border Protection officer at the St. Zacharie Port of Entry at approximately 9:15 a.m. to alert them to the bizarre sighting. By 9:40 a.m., the same workers had returned to the U.S. side with more intelligence: a third man had told them that two men in a gray Nissan parked on the Golden Road were asking passersby for fuel and Wi-Fi so they could contact the people they were supposed to pick up. At 10:13 a.m., that same third man called back -- the Nissan had turned up near his maple sugar shack at mile marker 80. A Border Patrol agent and the CBP officer loaded up a marked patrol vehicle and headed south on the Golden Road. At mile marker 90, they spotted fresh footprints in the soft dirt. At mile marker 87, they found the men themselves -- four individuals attempting to conceal themselves in roadside vegetation. Google Maps images of the area help show just how remote a location the supposed British hikers had found themselves in. "One of the four men was acting nervously," Hanton wrote in his affidavit. "The two officers took the four men into custody without incident." Although the Go Pro recording would show the men indisputably entered the U.S. illegally and intentionally, they initially claimed they were 'just going for a hike.' When questioned about their citizenship, all four told agents they were British citizens. They claimed they didn't know they had entered the United States, a claim the Go Pro recording revealed to be a lie. ? After being transported to the Jackman Border Patrol station, the men were identified as Ali Mohammed Ali Abdullah, 18, of Liverpool, England; Hameed Mohammed Nagi; Ibrahim Ayyub Khan; and Mohammed Sultan Saleh -- all British nationals, according to court documents. Their stories didn't hold up. Abdullah declined to answer questions. Nagi claimed he was just going on a hike with the group. Saleh echoed that line -- but federal agents had already found the GoPro footage on his phone, along with a series of telling Google searches conducted April 3: "bangor from my location," "boston from bangor," "new york from boston," and -- critically -- "is st zacharie border crossing still used the one near quebec golden road." That last search would appear to put to rest any claim that Saleh was unaware he had crossed an international border. The gray Nissan the maple sugar workers had described was still sitting near mile marker 80 when agents returned -- out of gas. Two men were inside. They identified themselves as U.S. citizens. Before the driver could fully exit the vehicle, a CBP officer observed him reach under the driver's seat. When agents checked, they found a loaded 9mm handgun. The two men in the Nissan were taken to Jackman as well, in connection with what the affidavit describes as "a suspected alien smuggling event." The passenger of the vehicle later admitted to investigators that the driver had intended to pick up one of the four men -- someone the driver said he had dropped off in the same Golden Road area approximately 30 days earlier, according to Homeland Security Investigations Special Agent Pierre Mathieu, who briefed Hanton. A forensic review of the driver's cell phone found text messages with an individual believed to be one of the four men, discussing expected arrival times and pickup logistics, according to the court filing. Federal prosecutors' motion for pretrial detention adds a further wrinkle to the story. Abdullah, identified as the lead defendant in the criminal complaints, had previously run afoul of U.S. immigration authorities. His application to extend his U.S. visa was denied in March 2025, and he departed the country in May 2025, the motion states. Prosecutors allege that Canadian authorities had recorded his arrival in Canada on April 1, 2026 -- two days before the Maine crossing -- traveling on a United Kingdom passport. "Law enforcement authorities are attempting to ascertain the purpose of his travel to Maine," the motion states. All four men are charged with one count each of Entry Without Inspection, a Class B misdemeanor under 8 U.S.C. § 1325(a)(1), which carries a maximum sentence of six months in federal prison and a $5,000 fine. The case is assigned to U.S. Magistrate Judge John C. Nivison. Abdullah appeared before the court on April 7 and waived his right to both a preliminary hearing and a detention hearing, consenting to remain in federal custody pending trial. The court accepted his waiver and ordered him detained. Trial is scheduled to begin June 3, 2026, before Magistrate Judge Nivison. Pretrial motions are due April 21. The three co-defendants -- Nagi, Khan, and Saleh -- have related cases pending in the same district. You 're receiving The Robinson Report for free. I’ve watched MAGA extremists at the local level push book bans and inject politics into our classrooms. It’s all to distract from what really matters: **making sure our kids can learn, grow, and feel supported.** That’s one of the reasons I first decided to run. Right now, Donald Trump and Linda McMahon are working to dismantle the Department of Education as we know it. **And here at home, Congressman Jeff Crank is backing that effort.** He’s said we don’t need a federal Department of Education and supports legislation to eliminate it. **Let’s be clear about what that means.**
---
* It puts support for special needs students at risk.
* It threatens resources that help schools serve every child.
* It shifts responsibility without guaranteeing accountability.

body:
The SAVE America Act would save the midterms, but not if the Senate doesn’t pass it
| Patriot, I'll be honest with you. I've been watching the debate over the SAVE America Act in Washington — and while I'm cheering for it to pass, I've been in this fight long enough to know something most people won't say: **We cannot afford to wait on Washington to save our elections.** While politicians debate, the Democrat ground game does not stop. Their voter registration staffers are at their tables right now. Their ballot chasers are making their calls. Their door knockers are hitting their lists. _And if we are not doing the same thing — right now — we are falling behind._ **I know this because I've lived it.** In 2024, my team spent over a year embedded on the ground in Pennsylvania before Election Day. We helped register hundreds of thousands of new Republican voters. We chased down every outstanding mail-in ballot we legally could. We drove voters to the polls on Election Day. **That is why Pennsylvania went red.** Not because of any law. Not because of any court ruling. Because of boots on the ground, day after day, doing the unglamorous, exhausting, absolutely essential work of grassroots organizing.

High prices are on everyone’s minds. Families are working hard and still feeling like they're falling behind. name: Heidi Ganahl
subject: The Mountain Minute: 4/9/2026
body:
Colorado fought scrutiny—until a lawsuit forced a cleanup
| | | | [](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**
| | Hi friends!
Listen to the Mountain Minute podcast on [YouTube](https://link.email.joinrmv.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.joinrmv.). Here is a summary of today's top stories:
🏛️ **Under the Golden Dome...** Lawmakers are considering [a new fee on homeowners insurance policies](https://link.email.joinrmv.) to fund a $20 million grant program for hail-resistant roofs as premiums—up about 65% in five years—continue to rise, though a similar effort failed previously.

🏔️ **Here in Colorado...** Boulder’s climate goals face [feasibility concerns](https://link.email.joinrmv.) alongside warnings of potential power shortages, while a [federal review of Colorado’s wolf reintroduction program](https://link.email.joinrmv.) is underway amid livestock conflicts. Lakewood voters [rejected higher-density zoning changes](https://link.email.joinrmv.), education debates have emerged over [classroom neutrality](https://link.email.joinrmv.), and the attorney general race shifted as [Republican David Willson entered late](https://link.email.joinrmv.) emphasizing law enforcement and accountability.
Election oversight is also back in focus after renewed attention to a [lawsuit-driven cleanup of Colorado’s voter rolls](https://link.email.joinrmv.), including the removal of hundreds of thousands of inactive or ineligible names and continued debate over how much outside scrutiny the state’s election system should face.
🇺🇸**On the National Stage...** President Trump announced a [two-week ceasefire with Iran](https://link.email.joinrmv.) tied to reopening the Strait of Hormuz, while newly uncovered records show a [federal disinformation initiative tested tools targeting U.S. media](https://link.email.joinrmv.).
This is your Mountain Minute for Thursday, April 9, 2026.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Colorado fought scrutiny—until a lawsuit forced a cleanup](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** BY RMV EDITORIAL BOARD, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
[](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
Back in 2019, Colorado’s voter rolls were already showing the problem—if anyone in charge had been willing to look at them.
Forty counties had more registered voters than eligible citizens. Call it whatever you want—but it’s not normal.
That wasn’t a partisan claim. It wasn’t a social media theory. It was data.
And for a long time, it just sat there. No press conference. No urgency. No statewide fix.
Then something happened. Someone sued.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**
|
---
**[He lost once. Now he’s back: Why David Willson jumped into Colorado’s AG race late](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
* ******Late entry shakes up AG race:** Republican David Willson entered the attorney general race just days before the state assembly, saying he was urged to run and emphasizing a message of balancing compassion with law enforcement.

* **Background rooted in law, military, and national security:** Willson spent 20 years as a JAG officer and later worked with the NSA, followed by a decade defending parents in neglect cases—shaping his focus on both accountability and real-world challenges in the justice system.

* **Campaign centered on investigations and election integrity:** He is calling for greater legal oversight, public investigations into election systems and school content, and a stronger enforcement approach, arguing the attorney general’s office should prioritize constitutional review over political agendas.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**
|
---

The only way we can continue to spread truth is with your support!
[DONATE TO ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
|
---
**[Suburban Voters In Lakewood Reject Multi Unit Housing Expansion Plan](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** [DENVER GAZETTE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
* **********Lakewood voters overturn zoning changes:** Residents voted to repeal city-approved “density” measures that would have expanded multifamily housing, restoring prior zoning rules focused on single-family neighborhoods.

* **Clear margin signals strong opposition:** Early results showed decisive support for repeal across all four ballot questions, reflecting broad voter resistance to the changes.

* **Debate highlights broader housing divide:** Supporters argued the changes would increase housing options and align with state mandates, while opponents raised concerns about neighborhood character, infrastructure, and local control—fueling a larger regional debate over density policies.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**
|
---
**ONLY ON ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE ⤵️ **
**[](https://link.email.joinrmv.)****[From Kazakhstan to Colorado: Secretary of State candidate James Wiley’s plan to scrap electronic voting machines](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**
**[](https://link.email.joinrmv.)****BY JEN SCHUMANN | STATE | APRIL 7** _James Wiley was 7 on Election Night 2000. He remembers the decorations from his birthday staying up for two more weeks while the country waited to find out who had won. He didn’t understand hanging chads or voting machines. At the time, he was living in Almaty, Kazakhstan, where his missionary family had been since he was three months old._ __
**[What Sets J.J. McKinzie Apart in Colorado’s Secretary of State Race](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**
**[](https://link.email.joinrmv.)****BY SHAINA COLE | COMMENTARY | APRIL 6** _J.J. McKinzie is one of four Republicans running for the open Secretary of State seat, and he is not running on name recognition. He is running on a resume that looks nothing like most politicians’. McKinzie spent more than 25 years inside some of the largest companies in the world, advising on regulatory compliance and operational efficiency._ ____
**[Colorado’s ‘politically homeless’ voters: Who’s showing up—and who’s not](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** **BY RMV STAFF | STATE | APRIL 6** _Erin Brantley doesn’t see Colorado politics from a campaign office or a party meeting. She sees it in real time—through thousands of conversations with voters who aren’t sure where they belong, or whether their vote even matters._**[](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**__

name: Letitia James
subject: I will never back down.
body:
I will not be intimidated.
#
Donald Trump and his political enablers in his administration are coming after me — _again._
The Trump administration just filed “new” criminal referrals to the Department of Justice targeting me, but there’s nothing new about them. They’re the same baseless allegations that courts and grand juries have already rejected.
You can probably guess why. _**Because I did my job — and won.**_
I took on Donald Trump and held him accountable for defrauding the people of New York.
Now, he’s escalating his revenge campaign, abusing his power and weaponizing our justice system for political retribution.
**I will not be intimidated. I will never give in to bullies. And I will never back down from holding the president accountable.**
My oath is to justice and to the people I serve. I intend to continue defending the rule of law and protecting New Yorkers, no matter how rich or powerful the opposition may be. That’s why I’m running for reelection as Attorney General of New York.

body:
My father and I couldn’t do this without patriots like you. Open this note of gratitude. |
Fellow American, _**it's Don Jr**_. I wanted to take a moment to **express my heartfelt gratitude** for **your unwavering support**. My father and I know that this fight **isn't possible without patriots like you** who are willing to stand up for what's right.

name: Forward Party
subject: Our First Congressional Endorsements of 2026
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Forward Party and not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee
body:
We’ve officially kicked off our 2026 congressional endorsements, and this first slate says a lot about where this movement is headed.

| | | [ ](www.forwardparty.com)
---
### Peter —
We’ve officially kicked off our 2026 congressional endorsements, and this first slate says a lot about where this movement is headed. These are not typical candidates. They are leaders who have built careers solving real problems, working in their communities, and stepping up because they believe the system should work better than it does today. They come from different backgrounds and different regions, but they share a commitment to practical leadership, accountability, and getting things done. Looking across this first group of endorsed congressional candidates, a few things stand out. These are problem solvers first. They have spent their careers in service, whether in business, public service, or their local communities, focused on outcomes instead of ideology. They are also stepping forward at a moment when most Americans feel like the system is not listening. Nearly half the country identifies as independent, yet the system still forces binary choices between the legacy parties. Just as important, they are willing to run anyway. One of the biggest challenges in our politics today is not just who wins, but who never runs in the first place. Too many capable leaders look at the current system and opt out. These candidates are choosing to step up. [](https://www.forwardparty.com/candidates/?e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_98a&n=1) _**Click the image for more information on each of our 2026 endorsed candidates so far.**_ This election is bigger than any single race. We are operating in a system where trust in government is low, competition is limited, and outcomes are too often driven by small, partisan primaries instead of the broader public. That combination produces exactly what voters are tired of: more division, less problem solving, and fewer real choices. At the same time, there is a clear opportunity. Most Americans are not asking for more extremes. They are asking for leaders who can work across differences, focus on solutions, and represent the full community, not just one side of it. This first slate also reflects something bigger about how change can actually happen. It does not take a majority to shift how Congress works. A small group of independent minded leaders who are focused on solutions instead of party can become a deciding force and help bridge divides. That is how incentives begin to shift toward cooperation instead of conflict and negotiation instead of gridlock. This is just the beginning. This first group of congressional endorsements is one step in a much broader effort, with many more endorsements to come across federal, statewide, and local elections. The goal is to build a durable pipeline of leaders who reflect the country as it actually is and give voters more credible choices at every level. That work is already underway. Earlier in the cycle, we made our first endorsement of the year with gubernatorial candidate Rick Bennett in Maine, a leader who has consistently demonstrated what it looks like to put voters ahead of party and govern with integrity. That endorsement helped set the tone for what we are building, and this first congressional slate continues that momentum. At its core, this effort is about something simple. American politics should reflect the American people. Right now, it does not, but it can. By supporting candidates like these, leaders who are independent minded, solutions oriented, and accountable, we are helping create a system where voters have real choices again. This is an important step forward, and there is much more to come. **Please forward this to your friends, family, and coworkers. It helps us introduce them to Forward and to what we are building. Also consider inviting them to one of our upcoming events listed below. We'd love to meet them.**

body:
Trump called into Fox News to sound the alarm. The Senate majority is everything — and it's not guaranteed. |
Peter,

Trump called into The Five on Fox News and said it plain:

**"We have to keep the majority, otherwise all of the things we've done are going to go down the tubes."**

That's it. That's the whole stakes of 2026.

| Peter,

THE UNIVERSITY OF MICHIGAN ARE NATIONAL CHAMPIONS! **🏀**

Now, I’ll be honest... I’m a Michigan State alum.

So yeah, watching our Sweet Sixteen loss to UConn? Brutal. I was fully prepared for a Michigan State vs. UMich final. (And we all know how that would’ve gone **😏**)

But hey, can’t win them all.

Surely this isn't the "greatness" we were promised from this administration?
Peter, _Andy said it best:_ [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/129131249/613393249/57398372?refcode=em26_260409_costs_fndd_gq_act___ITTPAC_ettx&utm_campaign=em26_260409_costs_fndd_gq_act___ITTPAC_ettx&utm_medium=email&refcode2=5305c3fa-4a34-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMTAzNjMiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNTMwNWMzZmEtNGEzNC1mMTExLThlZjItMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=-AoxPs3i-0t-N-3UBci6PliTe0Tep5tm-udzmOicY3s=) When Americans sit down to pay their bills at the end of the month and wonder how it all adds up, it's stressful, it's exhausting, and it's not what anyone was promised. What makes it worse is that Trump’s allies in Washington are pretending they don't know the hardships their constituents are facing.

**Yet, they know exactly what's happening.**

Across the country, people are speaking up at town halls, in their communities, face-to-face with the very officials who are supposed to represent them—and they're being clear: **Things aren't working.**

But instead of trying to find commonsense solutions, we're seeing inaction from elected Republicans in the White House and Congress. That's not how leadership works.

Leadership means listening when people tell you they're struggling, doing something about it, and making decisions that actually help families get ahead—not policies that make life harder or push the basics further out of reach.

At In This Together PAC, we operate on the basic principle that every American deserves leaders who take their responsibilities as elected officials seriously, and who don't ignore the problem, but get to work fixing it with action, not excuses. clean_body: Surely this isn't the "greatness" we were promised from this administration? Peter, Andy said it best: = When Americans sit down to pay their bills at the end of the month and wonder how it all adds up, it's stressful, it's exhausting, and it's not what anyone was promised. What makes it worse is that Trump’s allies in Washington are pretending they don't know the hardships their constituents are facing. Yet, they know exactly what's happening. Across the country, people are speaking up at town halls, in their communities, face-to-face with the very officials who are supposed to represent them—and they're being clear: Things aren't working. But instead of trying to find commonsense solutions, we're seeing inaction from elected Republicans in the White House and Congress. That's not how leadership works. Leadership means listening when people tell you they're struggling, doing something about it, and making decisions that actually help families get ahead—not policies that make life harder or push the basics further out of reach. In a Texas ICE detention center, the unthinkable has become a bloodsport: guards were caught in a ghoulish scandal, placing cold-blooded bets on which detainees would be the next to take their own lives. This isn't just a failure of oversight; it is a descent into absolute MAGA moral depravity, where human souls are treated as gambling chips in a state-sponsored house of horrors. But while the headlines are horrifying, there is a strategic way to fight back. **The federal government cannot run a police state without local pipes, local roads, and local permits.** By electing leaders who utilize "home rule" powers - like denying utility access, enacting strict zoning bans, and passing non-cooperation mandates - we can make the construction of new ICE facilities logistically and financially impossible. **Local Democracy Project is that guardrail. We recruit and train the city councilors and state legislators who have the literal power to pull the plug on federal overreach. Protests voice our outrage, but local policy builds the wall that stops this regime in its tracks.** _From city councils to state legislatures, we are building a wall of leaders who will say NO to this regime. name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: Here are a few ways the Trump family has made money off of his presidency:
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=2846%2E4032634%2EPUdk1L)
---
Donald Trump and his family have turned the presidential office into a hotbed of corruption. According to a new report from the _New Yorker_ , the Trump family has accumulated over **$3 billion while being president.** How is this possible, you might ask? It’s corruption, plain and simple. Here are _a few_ of the ways the Trump family may have made money off his presidency:
* Trump has brought in an estimated **$125 million** by hosting campaign events and essentially selling access at his Mar-A-Lago resort.
* At least **$27.7 million** has been estimated to come in through his private online store that sells campaign-style merch (Traditionally, campaign merch will support the campaign. But the sale of this Trump merch goes to Trump directly.)
* Trump’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner, was a walking conflict of interest as he informed policies in the Middle East while also having business and real estate interests in the region. It was estimated that his private equity firm made **$320 million** through private equity deals with the Saudis — possibly exchanged in an effort to curry favor or receive favorability.
* What’s more, the Trump Organization has also closed on hotel, resort, and golf club deals worth at least **$105.8 million** with the Saudis, and made a **$40 million** deal to license a Trump-branded resort in Hanoi.
* Remember when Qatar gifted Trump a private jet? That was worth at least **$150 million**. (Trump was able to accept this gift through his Presidential Library fund — **I’ve got a bill to close this loophole.**)
* And this is a biggie: Trump has been able to wield his executive authority by suing large companies and receiving settlements through the Trump Presidential Library fund. He sued ABC for defamation, and they agreed to pay **$15 million** to settle. He went after Meta for kicking him off their platforms following the January 6th insurrection, and they settled for **$22 million**. He went after X for the same thing, and they reportedly settled for **$10 million**. Oh yeah, and Paramount conveniently settled his defamation suit against them for **$16 million** around the same time they started seeking merger approval from his Administration. My bill would put an end to these settlements, too.
* I’m sure you saw lots and lots (and lots) of marketing materials for Amazon’s movie about Melania Trump. Amazon paid $40 million for the rights to the Melania documentary, with **$28 million** going directly to Melania Trump. Meanwhile, Amazon and Jeff Bezos have huge financial stakes in decisions pending before the Trump administration. **I’m investigating whether Amazon violated federal bribery laws.**
* Yes, as a sitting president, Trump shares erratic and problematic content on Truth Social. Did you know that Trump’s media shell company — Trump Media & Technology Group — owns a majority stake in the platform and has gained him an estimated **$25 million**? He’s got a financial incentive for his official presidential communications to exclusively be shared on Truth Social.
* Donald Trump Jr. is currently a partner at a venture-capital firm he co-founded called 1789 Capital, which has acquired minority stakes in a number of companies that are affected by the decisions of the federal government, including defense contractors — gaining him an estimated **$19.6 million**.
* Oh, and the crypto of it all...The Trump family has made over **$2 billion dollars** from their involvement in cryptocurrencies. That includes selling NFTs of Trump looking like Superman, selling digital tokens like $TRUMP and $MELANIA, and running crypto firms that execute lucrative deals with wealthy families from the Gulf or invest in A.I. data centers. All of this happened as Trump has led the fight to deregulate the crypto industry.

**All in all, the _New Yorker_ estimates a total of $3.4 billion that the Trump family has potentially made off of his presidency (from what they have tracked so far).** This is all sickening. The American people should have complete confidence that their president is making decisions with only one factor in mind: the public interest. Not his bank accounts, not his family fortune, not the value of his cryptocurrencies. That’s why I’m fighting Trump’s corruption and grift every day in the Senate — and why I’ve proposed the most ambitious set of anti-corruption reforms since Watergate. We’ve got to take back our Congressional majorities to put a strong check on this corrupt Administration — and then work to put some real measures in place to clean up the corruption in our politics and hold grifters accountable. [**I’m going to stay on this. If you’re sick and tired of seeing the Trump family rake in billions as they make life more expensive for working families, pitch in $28 or anything you can to fuel our fight to get corruption out of our politics.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3575?amount=28&t=8&akid=2846%2E4032634%2EPUdk1L)

name: Evan Hunt
subject: A constituent of mine is sitting in a Mississippi jail cell for following the law.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Elect Evan Hunt
body:
Share his story far and wide | | [ ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMYE5U9NTRbOMLNsSMiwuHsSrn4JnyYtk1EREaCYHldIw2Es-lCsKe-k7RYeRErCjUmpL6YWg0aqprxBCSlqaUKjL6uf8EDq6vQVEaFZEFWaTvOKtPnFc2PEalY2SnM4_7TdSMdP6KvOfffozTZ_rgLvHyDEmYu_XQ7pmRQqjmq-zRaRkejwHE68US97azSxtCTe-4dKAZ14bDCyp8o2xnLrlB-mVHhnToNNOzPvdQb_gJxQBfjvMm55-YgmnqJrCsmUBwQFAeODKqTqIFei3tQIknrQsqcOBCJ9jAbqh4xad/4pn/ixutPzNNTLOOe68iogZs9g/h0/h001.c2oBBxhkPSlnRsWjGC4pI-cN18D4M_SHzGcBQ9ULJBg)
---
Peter, I want to tell you about Rafael and Heather Allambaro, who live right here in TX-03.
---
| [ ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt8yrIxAhEjI10Vy7fAJvyx3F7YuHAMDJ9LGZSxWwXyE-lTDPzuLUnXszABNdDQdiqwSWWObOB13Bx-EM3uGh-_vPZaP_2HxMshWorf83jPjm5HqSbofWEO1qoMQU2M2N_ENUVvtAvPe6ZAMLFItY8BT8R62SJrd-hzzObR8csedPgqb5yfr54bKIbOf_9clVeX5mCbmi_9lw-nqTHxCUe_mYXerqW3WtIKMLXZrNAHfmLhy8M6Vi_RJTH_dF3dxCc0sF2nlRnLqMTjzgMfXj7bKIOE4Pobr1DzRVQry1VncCnvqdV8-v1SEn88mUXhJpuOrL0tAXhlY1Adtm34etHqNg/4pn/ixutPzNNTLOOe68iogZs9g/h1/h001.KrlvyxoE1o7Wwwkhs8qJJF-k9U_YGXUCzGHwJgLe0dg)
---
Rafael fled Venezuela after organizing against the Maduro regime made it too dangerous to stay. He did exactly what asylum seekers are supposed to do: presented himself to border authorities, requested asylum, was vetted, and was found to have a credible fear for his life. He was released on humanitarian parole, given a Social Security number, work authorization, and a Texas driver's license. He checked in with ICE every single year and built a life here the way our system told him to. He and Heather married last June.
---
| [ ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt8yrIxAhEjI10Vy7fAJvyx3F7YuHAMDJ9LGZSxWwXyE-leGW_lwYgnS-vpX583q_figQXrku1V73jV0TF-Vd9x8j-KASGj0p1PwBNydfTPYRsQ01oMdFTESXFUBoKl1AhFUeSaKqNX5l_nxmlQ98u_iYxNvhNg671Wo4rlUMtvls5_iUVc_5q-lHc_uLTQuTZEz92l_clh7j8bbFGYazM5A6CzY35TiatONspprQt_K4s0EF97eFUWIMJtEFa0flZdlNDZU0zLStI9SIc7VETnmZrK55chq41qZtZOudiobDE1CUwUQlHR13cMyxi5CD4wPn0LIqORLOowQae5PmIh4s/4pn/ixutPzNNTLOOe68iogZs9g/h2/h001.jQUwXasjuQUlThDR9dlWtoZez4oj6TcjJtHYeBNAig8)
---
They filed the legal paperwork for his green card and sat for their interview the day before Thanksgiving. The very next day the government froze processing for people from countries like Venezuela and put his case on hold overnight. On January 15th, Rafael showed up to his routine annual ICE check-in and was detained on the spot. **He is now in a detention center in Mississippi without cause, sleeping in a cell behind bars.** [**Help us build a campaign that fights for every Rafael in this district and every family carrying this weight right now.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt8yrIxAhEjI10Vy7fAJvyx3F7YuHAMDJ9LGZSxWwXyE-lasWG9_v7xVrlVSqLFPk_nGbjawgdxpG-ZLXechBQeswl-vNxmxXn3GoTdcZiMNNZc5LLDcmKB9-mWdOIBJw2FS-CjpLdqgm2afH--cuclsBUtg4UvAHoHJaATcQE1u5q1YBqEe0roKuKeuBVPoZVg19A2Qothj4uXTg3sLKz43wqcZemGq7zLM-B7uxerbbRLDNc4frdgr4-0e3_nJJkoa6mRKB-h8Ek_RgeHSMg00oJ8Sc5ita835NvtNPvUwGqgp-JuG-VP3ph2kNn_rvNWlDhj_4g0q-PouzxYbfc4xY/4pn/ixutPzNNTLOOe68iogZs9g/h3/h001.QQhHWkUpHpvhbfd5e3FqtZNEC5QX1qDG_NyFSwCIujE) Heather has contacted her representatives - including our current congressman, Keith Self. My opponent likes to talk about the rule of law and immigrants "doing things the right way", but he, of course, has done nothing to help his own constituent wrongly detained by ICE. Worse, shortly after Heather contacted his office, Rafael was transferred out of state. Self not only let it happen, he celebrates the very enforcement priorities that put Rafael in that cell and has spent his career demonizing the communities and countries these families come from. Service Before Self means using every tool available, including this platform, to fight for constituents who are doing everything right and getting punished for it anyway. The fix here is simple. clean_body: Share his story far and wide | | Peter, I want to tell you about Rafael and Heather Allambaro, who live right here in TX-03. | Rafael fled Venezuela after organizing against the Maduro regime made it too dangerous to stay. He did exactly what asylum seekers are supposed to do: presented himself to border authorities, requested asylum, was vetted, and was found to have a credible fear for his life. He was released on humanitarian parole, given a Social Security number, work authorization, and a Texas driver's license. He checked in with ICE every single year and built a life here the way our system told him to. He and Heather married last June. | They filed the legal paperwork for his green card and sat for their interview the day before Thanksgiving. The very next day the government froze processing for people from countries like Venezuela and put his case on hold overnight. On January 15th, Rafael showed up to his routine annual ICE check-in and was detained on the spot. He is now in a detention center in Mississippi without cause, sleeping in a cell behind bars. Heather has contacted her representatives - including our current congressman, Keith Self. My opponent likes to talk about the rule of law and immigrants "doing things the right way", but he, of course, has done nothing to help his own constituent wrongly detained by ICE. Worse, shortly after Heather contacted his office, Rafael was transferred out of state. Self not only let it happen, he celebrates the very enforcement priorities that put Rafael in that cell and has spent his career demonizing the communities and countries these families come from. It still strikes me as odd that Republicans beat the Democrats on the Internet in 2024. Not long ago, Obama seemed to personify excellent political advocacy over the Internet. But then in 2024, we spent more money than the Republicans on digital communications, and we still lost miserably.
The story of all that is too long for this post, but I'm happy to report we're finally learning how to change things. This week in [Puck](https://substack.com/redirect/e4ad9046-47ee-47b8-95ac-7ab7657a3857?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (which is unfortunately paywalled), Peter Hamby wrote about the efforts of a Democratic Super PAC called Priorities USA, which is doing groundbreaking work reaching young men in Ohio. (Potentially the state that will determine control of the Senate later this year).
I have been working with Priorities for about a year, and their approach is unique. Like a business, they invented their own tools to better map and measure what's happening online. One of those tools, Warbler, allows us to target our ads across the ecosystem in a much more sophisticated and data-driven way. As Hamby described it:
> Warbler is essentially a dashboard that maps how different voting groups are spending their time on platforms with different content categories. ... In small settings, [they] ask voters for screen recordings and interrogate them about their social media behaviors. ... Afterward ... "we literally have them share their screen, and walk us through what's recommended to them. Why would you click this and not this? Why does this creator come across as credible to you? Why does this thumbnail seem like garbage?" .... **Warbler allows political advertisers to go even more niche than the targeting buckets offered by Google and other Big Tech platforms**.
The importance of a tool like this is that it will help candidates break the habits we learned filming 30-second TV spots. TV spots generally come across as inauthentic online. Yet that's increasingly where people are. Priorities has shown that YouTube now reaches 80 percent of voters (86 percent of Latinos), compared to just 62 percent for cable and broadcast television. So why aren't we creating digital-first content?
That is the goal of the research Priorities is doing in Ohio. Here's how Hamby describes their creative attack on Senator Jon Husted, who is being challenged by Sherrod Brown (again, in a race that could determine control of the Senate):
> In the coming weeks, gamers in Ohio--mostly apolitical young men--will start to see a certain ad on YouTube ... [that] looks and sounds a lot like the short interstitial ads that social media-addled users have grown accustomed to: a random guy wearing headphones sitting next to a podcast mic and talking straight-to-camera; bold, rapid-fire text; quick-cut edits; and a loud, fast-talking voiceover. "If you play video games, you might've noticed your power bills are just a wee bit higher these days," the narrator explains. "Well, you can thank this guy, Ohio Senator Jon Husted." ....
> In a brisk 20 seconds, the spot outlines Husted's connections to a bribery scandal involving FirstEnergy, one of Ohio's largest energy utilities. ... "[Husted] sides with the power companies while our bank accounts get cooked," the ad says, before ending with, "Oh! I almost forgot about the Epstein stuff. But we're out of time, so just Google it."
Not an ad you would see on television, but one perfectly suited for _today 's _media environment.
Priorities will be especially active in US House races this fall. If you're interested in helping to fund this kind of work, as opposed to the usual TV ads that pay a lot to campaign consultants but reach a diminishing number of voters, reach out to me [here](https://substack.com/redirect/9fecd076-d422-4b6e-8159-fc620628497a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (clamb@priorities.org). We need your help.

| Dear Peter,

JUST IN: A federal court has paused Louisiana's attempt to make it harder for people around the country to get an abortion. This is good news—but only for now. Louisiana has _already_ appealed the ruling. [And there's a bigger catch: the stay only happened because the Trump administration asked the FDA to re-review mifepristone—and that review is a total sham.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/129132011/613396015/1824768205?sourceid=1151269&utm_campaign=medab&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=medab&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3YTNkYTU3Zi00ZTM0LWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ooCa8nABXU3jxxy4UDpJigK5lVvaoVwAOwUVc7_6v-0=&emci=8ce98778-4e34-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=7a3da57f-4e34-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=954237) | [FIGHT BACK](https://click.everyaction.com/k/129132012/613396016/1824768205?sourceid=1151269&utm_campaign=medab&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=medab&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3YTNkYTU3Zi00ZTM0LWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ooCa8nABXU3jxxy4UDpJigK5lVvaoVwAOwUVc7_6v-0=&emci=8ce98778-4e34-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=7a3da57f-4e34-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=954237)
---
Mifepristone is safe. Mifepristone is effective. Full stop. It's been used by more than 7.5 million people in the U.S., is backed by hundreds of studies, and has been FDA-approved for 25 years. _There is no medical or scientific reason to restrict it._ This "review" is nothing more than a thinly veiled attempt to lay the groundwork for nationwide restrictions on medication abortion.

Abortion pills are safe, effective, and a true gamechanger for access across the country—which is exactly why the anti-abortion movement is targeting medication abortion. [Make no mistake: restricting mifepristone isn't about safety. clean_body: Why a sham FDA "review" just put mifepristone back in danger | | | | | | Dear Peter, JUST IN: A federal court has paused Louisiana's attempt to make it harder for people around the country to get an abortion. This is good news—but only for now. Louisiana has already appealed the ruling. | Mifepristone is safe. Mifepristone is effective. Full stop. It's been used by more than 7.5 million people in the U.S., is backed by hundreds of studies, and has been FDA-approved for 25 years. There is no medical or scientific reason to restrict it. This "review" is nothing more than a thinly veiled attempt to lay the groundwork for nationwide restrictions on medication abortion. Abortion pills are safe, effective, and a true gamechanger for access across the country—which is exactly why the anti-abortion movement is targeting medication abortion. This fight is far from over, and we need you with us. Every time we speak up about mifepristone's safety, every time we push back on junk science, it matters.
